proposals.spec_says: evict_next() delegates victim selection to the eviction policy (`identify_next_to_evict(pool_id)`), then removes that slot and frees its allocation; there is no shard round-robin counter
proposals.code_does: Victim popped from the policy (lib.rs:452) before the pool write lock (:465). Returns Some(key) and bumps evictions even when no slot was freed (:467-473). Recycled LRU indices without a generation (lru_list.rs:38-46,143) let remove(K) (lib.rs:511) delete another key's node, so that key can never be evicted.
proposals.code_change: Take the pool write guard before identify_next_to_evict (lock order pool -> policy, as in insert/remove/clear). Return Some(key) and count an eviction only when a slot was actually removed. First add a test that reproduces the interleaving.

proposals.spec_says: Concurrent access from 16+ threads does not deadlock or corrupt state
proposals.code_does: get/touch/batch_touch drop the pool lock, then call the policy with a copied handle. A racing clear empties the LRU node vector (lru_list.rs:147-153), so move_to_back indexes out of bounds (lru_list.rs:70-71) and panics while holding the policy's pool mutex (eviction-policy-lru/src/lib.rs:84-85), poisoning it. No multi-threaded test exists.
proposals.code_change: Either (a) call the policy while still holding the pool read guard (and reword NFR-002), or (b) bounds-check plus a generation-checked EvictionHandle in eviction-policy-lru/interfaces (this also fixes P3). Add the 16-thread mixed stress test from tasks.md:20.

proposals.spec_says: All operations check initialized flag before proceeding
proposals.code_does: Checked in 14 operations; insert size==0 and batch_touch([]) return before the check; is_dma_capable and telemetry_snapshot never check it; initialize checks it inverted

edits.old: | FR-023 | All operations check initialized flag before proceeding | Implementation |
edits.new: | FR-023 | Every operation that reads or changes pool state checks the initialized flag first, and returns its "not initialized" result when the flag is unset (`NotInitialized` for `insert`/`remove`/`clear`; `None`, `false`, `0`, an empty `Vec`, or a no-op for the others). Exceptions: `insert` rejects `size == 0` with `InvalidSize`, and `batch_touch` returns on an empty slice, before the check; `is_dma_capable()` and `telemetry_snapshot()` do not check the flag (their results are well-defined before initialization); `initialize()` rejects an already-set flag | Implementation |

proposals.spec_says: tracks eviction count, write-lock contention count, and read-lock contention count; a failed try_read/try_write first attempt bumps the corresponding lock-contention counter before blocking
proposals.code_does: Write contention counted in insert/evict_next/remove only; read contention in get/batch_touch only; clear/peek/touch/contains/capacity/used/free_capacity not counted; evictions bumped whenever the policy returns a victim

edits.old: | FR-027 | When compiled with the optional `telemetry` feature, the component tracks eviction count, write-lock contention count, and read-lock contention count | Implementation *(backfilled)* |
edits.new: | FR-027 | When compiled with the optional `telemetry` feature, the component tracks eviction count (one per `evict_next` call for which the policy returned a victim), write-lock contention count (measured in `insert`, `remove`, `evict_next`), and read-lock contention count (measured in `get`, `batch_touch`); other lock acquisitions (`clear`, `peek`, `touch`, `contains`, `capacity`, `used`, `free_capacity`) are not measured | Implementation *(backfilled)* |

edits.old: When the `telemetry` feature is enabled, a failed `try_read`/`try_write` first attempt bumps the corresponding lock-contention counter before blocking.
edits.new: When the `telemetry` feature is enabled, the measured paths (`insert`, `remove`, `evict_next` for the write lock; `get`, `batch_touch` for the read lock) first try `try_write`/`try_read` and, if that fails, bump the corresponding lock-contention counter before blocking.

edits.old: | NFR-005 | Allocator uses BTreeMap for O(log n) first-fit search | Implementation |
edits.new: | NFR-005 | Allocator keeps free regions in a BTreeMap keyed by offset: map updates and coalescing lookups are O(log k), and the first-fit search (`allocate`, `can_allocate`) is a linear scan, O(k), over the k free regions in offset order | Implementation |
